ships.checker_verdict: PASS after one fix cycle. THREE independent checkers, none given a prior verdict, all on a DIFFERENT MODEL from the maker. PASS 1 primary, verbatim: "VERDICT: PARTIAL - matcher is correct (0/56,766 divergences, 46/46, 64/64, 14/14 e2e), secure (0 XSS, no proto-pollution), private (1 request, 0 cookies/storage), and premises are docs-accurate, but the page's absolute printed claim 'No input can make it hang' is false: a pasteable pattern/value pair produces a measured 5.6 s synchronous tab freeze because the linear-time Pike VM is still O(pattern x value) with no input-size guard." PASS 1 independent security adversary, verbatim: "VERDICT: FAIL - the freeze/hang objective produced multiple reproduced, measured defects (up to a full tab crash and multi-ten-second blocks well past the claimed 50ms ceiling), directly falsifying 'No input can make it hang,' while the XSS objective found nothing across an exhaustive, corpus-plus-hundreds-more sweep." It measured 7,755 ms on 5,000 files x 100 patterns (proven a true event-loop freeze: a screenshot 300 ms in timed out without returning a frame, and a 5 ms interval canary ticked 3 times where ~1,358 were due), 12,889 ms on 2,000-level nested YAML with no glob patterns at all, >90 s unfinished on '*?'x20000, and a TAB CRASH on a 20,000-level document. FIX CYCLE (one, as the contract allows): a work budget decremented by NFA states actually visited and checked inside the loop - unlike ship 002's failed static budget it measures work already done rather than predicting an exponential blow-up, so it cannot be satisfied and exceeded at once; out of budget yields CANNOT TELL, never a verdict. Plus encode-each-value-once, cached NFA scratch state, 1 MiB / 20k-line / 64-level parser limits, textLength checked before .value, clear-before-compute, 5,000-file and 4,096-char field caps, and the printed claim narrowed to what was actually proven. TARGETED RE-CHECK by a fresh adversary on the fix diff, verbatim: "VERDICT: PASS - every reported defect is fixed and neither the cached NFA scratch state nor the shared work budget produced any wrong verdict across ~69.5k RE2-differential and 6.1k bounded-vs-unbounded comparisons; the only residuals are two low-severity, sub-second UX/copy nuances." Before/after it measured: 7,755 ms -> 150 ms; 5,618 ms -> 188 ms; 9,675 ms -> 238 ms; >90 s -> 194 ms; 12.9 s / tab crash -> refused in 0 ms with no crash; 4,578 ms -> 0.9 ms. TWO RESIDUALS CARRIED, NOT FIXED (recorded rather than ground down - the contract allows one fix cycle, and changing code after the verdict would mean staging something unverified): (1) LOW stale-verdict-repaint - run() is synchronous so the clear() at its top is never painted before the compute, leaving the previous verdict as the last painted frame for up to ~0.67 s; DOM state is correct and a MutationObserver confirmed the old verdict is never re-inserted as current. (2) LOW copy-latency-scope - the copy's 'about a fifth of a second' is scoped to matching work and matches the measured ~0.23 s budget, but pattern compilation and YAML parsing sit outside the budget, so worst-case total latency is ~667 ms, roughly 3x what a reader may infer. VERIFIED SOUND across the round: 211,118 (pattern,value) pairs by the maker plus 56,766 and ~69,500 by two checkers against their OWN Go/RE2 builds of act, ZERO divergences in every set; 203,082 reuse comparisons proving the cached scratch state never changes an answer; 6,144 bounded-vs-unbounded comparisons proving the budget only ever declines, never flips a verdict; GitHub's published cheat sheet 46/46 and act's own corpus 64/64 run against the LIVE page; 5 GitHub filter premises re-verified against docs.github.com; ~870 XSS payloads across every field including the thrown-Error sink, 0 injections, 0 prototype pollution; no new RegExp on user input, sole innerHTML assignment is a static ''; every stated limit off-by-one correct and named in its refusal message; 1 external request (the cookieless Cloudflare beacon), 0 cookies, 0 storage. Live-URL unverified by this run (egress; no desktop bridge in a scheduled run) - and health.json does not exist because .github/workflows/ has not been added to the repo.

ships.one_liner: paste a CODEOWNERS file and the paths a PR touches — get the rule that wins per file, the owners requested, the rules that lost, and the lines GitHub silently skips
ships.gap_source_url: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners — EVERGREEN lane, why-now waived; the permanent demand is GitHub's own counter-intuitive precedence rule ("Order is important; the last matching pattern takes the most precedence") plus three documented footguns (! negation, [ ] ranges and \# escaping all silently do nothing) and silent line-skipping on any syntax error. Occupant hunt 2026-08-04, named and all CLI/library-shaped: hmarr/codeowners (Go CLI+lib), mszostok/codeowners-validator, orsinium-labs/owners, topfreegames/codeowners-verifier, nmusolino/codeowners, multimediallc/codeowners-plus (a GitHub Action replacement engine). GitHub's own web UI flags syntax errors but does not simulate a changed-file list against the rules. No free signup-free web page occupies the slot. Structural edge: free vs install-a-toolchain, paste vs checkout, whole file-list vs one path, explains the precedence decision, and runs entirely client-side so a private ownership map never leaves the browser.

ships.checker_verdict:
NOT A PASS. SIX independent checker verdicts across THREE fix cycles, none given a prior verdict, all on a DIFFERENT MODEL from the maker. Final two verdicts are both FAIL. This ship is not staged and must never be presented as verified.

ROUND 1 primary, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: PARTIAL" - `?` compiled to one BYTE where the reference consumes one RUNE, so `docs/report-v?.md` missed `docs/report-v<alpha>.md`. 147 mismatches in 27,534 adversarial pairs, 100% of them containing `?`.

ROUND 1 security adversary, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: FAIL" - "Pasting ... a single valid CODEOWNERS line consisting of 1,048,536 literal `a` characters ... freezes the tab for 2,029.9-3,893.7 ms" because parsing and compiling ran before the budget existed.

FIX CYCLE 1: `?` -> UTF-8 rune alternation; parse/compile charged; a wall-clock deadline added because measured step throughput varies ~7x by workload shape.

ROUND 2 targeted re-check, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: PARTIAL" - "Defect A ... is fixed cleanly and completely: 141,583 differential (pattern, path) pairs ... produced zero mismatches ... Defect B ... only partially fixed ... a block of 1,101-1,291 ms - meaningfully beyond both the page's own '~750 ms' claim ... Root cause: runes() ... and addThread() has no internal tick()/deadline check ... Critically, the safety property still held ... never a partial or wrong table."

FIX CYCLE 2 (authorised in session): metered runes() and addThread(); found the real cost underneath - literalBytes() allocated a TextEncoder ONCE PER LITERAL CHARACTER, 214 ms of a 526 ms parse - and fixed it with an ASCII fast path; added a 4,096-character pattern cap, because ~200 ms of the overshoot was garbage collection, which no work budget can bound. Worst measured block 1,291 ms -> 607 ms.

ROUND 3 timing adversary, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: FAIL" - "The worst block I achieved was a ~13.7-14.2 second main-thread freeze ... that ends not in the promised refusal banner but in an uncaught RangeError: Invalid string length - after which #result is left showing the stale, unrelated initial-preset table ... with zero error indication". Input: one rule with 40,000 owners against 5,000 one-character paths. "everything after that check (index.html:1099-1164, building the results-table HTML string) runs with no budget object at all."

ROUND 3 correctness adversary, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: FAIL" - "The page's own explicit, repeated claim of 'exactly two deliberate divergences' ... is false, and the falsification produces wrong owner/winner answers": parseFile split on a bare CR where Go's bufio.Scanner splits on \n only; the line trim used JavaScript's \s, which contains U+FEFF (Go's does not) and lacks U+0085 (Go's has it); error positions were rune indices where Go reports bytes. It also found the HARD-RULE breach: a personal name in a served file.

FIX CYCLE 3: render phase metered and bounded (20 owners/rule, 10 losing rules/file, 1,000 rows, each disclosed on the page; array+join instead of unbounded string concatenation; run() wrapped so a throw clears the result instead of leaving a stale answer). Line handling rewritten to bufio.Scanner semantics; Go's unicode.IsSpace set; byte-offset error positions. Personal name removed from every served file. Worst measured block 13,745 ms -> 563 ms.

ROUND 4 correctness, FRESH ADVERSARY, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: FAIL - live-URL unverified (egress)". Two grounds. (1) The personal name was STILL PUBLICLY REACHABLE in git history at commit 04e99c8, an ancestor of the pushed tip: "I fetched [repo URL removed — a raw file URL in a served file is how a handle leaked once before] directly and got HTTP 200 ... while control fetches ... all correctly 404 ... git history is additive: the earlier blob remains a permanently reachable, publicly-fetchable ancestor, so a plain `git diff main...ship/003-codeowners` misses it entirely." (2) A THIRD undisclosed divergence: "Go's bufio.Scanner has a hard 65,536-byte-per-token limit; a longer line makes Scan() fail with ErrTooLong, and since ParseFile never checks scanner.Err(), it silently returns only the rules parsed before that line, with a nil error - dropping that line and every rule after it, undetectably", while this port parses straight through and "confidently renders winner L3 after.txt -> @after-owner ... a silently wrong, confidently-displayed owner". Boundary pinned by binary search: 65,535 bytes kept, 65,536 dropped.

ROUND 4 timing, FRESH ADVERSARY, VERBATIM: "VERDICT: FAIL" - "The worst block achieved was 23,701 ms wall-clock (22,998.4 ms setInterval-canary max gap, 22,370.0 ms requestAnimationFrame max gap) ... from a CODEOWNERS file consisting of one line - `** @` followed by 100,000 `a` characters (a syntactically valid single owner token ... under 10% of the ... cap) - matched against 1,000 ordinary paths ... The 750 ms claim is FALSE." Three further defects: the path-list preprocessing loop runs unmetered BEFORE the MAX_PATHS check (499,999 one-character lines -> 8,408.7 ms); "'drawing is metered' is false; DOM construction/layout/paint are invisible to the budget" (810.4 ms dispatch-to-paint at exactly the page's own stated maximum); and the problems panel is unmetered (627.3 ms). It also confirmed: "I could not make the page show a stale or wrong answer - that specific promise held up under sustained, deliberate attack."

WHY THIS STOPS HERE. Three fix cycles, six verdicts, and each deeper probe found a worse instance of ONE class: the page bounds what it READS in aggregate but not the dimensions that drive work (line count, per-line length, per-token length), and nothing at all bounds what the browser does after JavaScript hands over. Patching stage by stage has not converged - it has taught the checkers where to look next. A fourth cycle in the same session would be grinding toward a soft PASS, which is the exact failure this contract exists to prevent. The fix is a DESIGN change, recorded as the rebuild constraint, not another patch.

VERIFIED SOUND ACROSS ALL SIX ROUNDS (what a rebuild inherits, and it is a lot): ~500,000 differential (pattern, path) pairs against independently built Go/RE2 reference binaries, ZERO divergences; 171/171 on the reference implementation's own corpus; 13/13 on GitHub's published example block with the documentation's expectation quoted, re-verified against a live fetch of the docs in four separate rounds; 2,500 generated multi-rule files / 37,204 rule lines / 30,985 paths end-to-end against the reference's own last-match-wins for winner AND skip-set, 0 mismatches, plus CRLF/bare-CR/BOM/U+0085/tab/NBSP cases; 1,097 'also matched and lost' sequences verified by iterative truncation, 0 mismatches; byte-exact error positions vs Go across 23 multi-byte and escaped cases; ~250 XSS payload-positions across six checkers with 0 injections and 0 dialogs (neither module contains a `throw`, so ship 002's thrown-Error sink cannot exist here); 0 prototype pollution across 18 probes; ~35,000 constrained-budget comparisons proving the budget only ever refuses and never flips an answer; all five input limits AND all three output limits off-by-one exact in both directions; truncation honesty proven adversarially (summary counts and the dead/shadowed classification are computed over the full dataset even when the table caps at 1,000 rows); 0 cookies, 0 storage, exactly two requests (the page and the cookieless beacon), no pasted content in any request; memory stable across 40 repeated runs; mobile 390px with 0 horizontal overflow; build reproducibility proven byte-for-byte; the render RangeError retested at 60,000 owners x 5,000 paths and now correct in 396 ms. Live-URL unverified by this run (egress); health.json does not exist because .github/workflows/ has not been added.

plain.what: A free web page: paste your CODEOWNERS file and the files a pull request touches, and it tells you exactly who GitHub will ask to review each one — and which of your rules it is quietly ignoring.
plain.solves: CODEOWNERS decides reviewers on every PR, but the LAST matching rule wins, not the most specific one — so teams routinely believe a rule is protecting a directory when a broader rule further down has been overriding it for months. Bad lines are skipped silently, with no warning anywhere.
plain.money: Not published. The matching engine is correct and heavily proven, and the page is secure and private — but its printed promise about never freezing is still not true, so it did not earn a stage. It returns as a rebuild with a design constraint rather than another patch.

ships.residual_defect: ONE ROOT CAUSE, FOUR SYMPTOMS. The page validates AGGREGATE input (total characters) but never the DIMENSIONS that actually drive work, and it cannot meter the browser at all once JavaScript hands over. (a) A single owner TOKEN has no length cap - MAX_OWNERS_SHOWN caps the COUNT, not the length - so `** @` + 100,000 'a' against 1,000 paths blocks 23,701 ms. The fix-cycle-3 comment named 'an owner list has no length cap' and then bounded the wrong axis of its own invariant. (b) The path-list split + per-line trim runs to completion BEFORE the MAX_PATHS check: 499,999 one-character lines blocks 8,408.7 ms and only then prints an accurate refusal. (c) innerHTML parse, layout and paint are outside any JS budget by construction; 810.4 ms dispatch-to-paint measured at exactly the maximum the page's own copy advertises as safe. (d) The problems panel collects entries unmetered (627.3 ms). Plus a correctness divergence of the same family: the reference silently drops a line >= 65,536 bytes AND every rule after it (Go bufio.Scanner ErrTooLong, unchecked by ParseFile); this port keeps going and shows a confidently wrong owner.
rebuild_constraint_design: 1. VALIDATE EVERY DIMENSION AT THE DOOR, before any split, trim, parse or compile - and count without materialising: total chars (already), LINE COUNT of both boxes (scan for \n with an early bail, never split first), per-line length, per-owner-token length, per-pattern length (already). Refuse naming the real number. Zero work before validation is the invariant; metering work you should not have started is the mistake this ship made three times.

2. BOUND THE OUTPUT BY CONSTRUCTION, not by budget. A JS tick cannot interrupt innerHTML parsing, layout or paint, so the DOM must be small before it is handed over: cap rows / owners / losing rules (already done) AND cap total rendered HTML length, then MEASURE PAINT - dispatch-to-double-rAF - not just a JS canary. The two disagree, and the user experiences the paint.

3. REPLICATE THE REFERENCE'S LIMITS, NOT ONLY ITS SEMANTICS. Go's bufio.Scanner drops any line >= 65,536 bytes and silently abandons the rest of the file. Either replicate that exactly (and show it, since it is a spectacular footgun worth surfacing to a user) or refuse such a line outright. Do not quietly diverge.
4. RE-DERIVE THE TIMING NUMBER FROM MEASUREMENT at the page's own stated maximum, and only after 1-3 hold. Do not print a ceiling before the architecture can honour it.

5. START FROM lib/checks/codeowners-oracle.json - 171 pairs, 13 documented cases, the line-skipping set, the Go differential recipe and six rounds of regression notes. The matcher itself is heavily proven; do not rebuild it.
